statement: Every smooth real plane quartic has at least four real bitangent lines, and this minimum is attained.

answer.qualification: Real lines are counted; contacts need not both be real. The classical classification is attributed to Zeuthen and Klein. This is not the minimum of totally real contact lines.

source.location: Theorem 1.7, PDF p.2; Table 1, PDF p.3

scope: Real projective bitangent lines to smooth real plane quartic curves; the two contact points may be real or a complex-conjugate pair.
notes:
Real lines are counted; contacts need not both be real. The classical classification is attributed to Zeuthen and Klein. This is not the minimum of totally real contact lines.

Originality audit: the real classification is attributed to Zeuthen; Plaumann–Sturmfels–Vinzant is the modern verification source retained in source. Minimum/maximum counts are consequences of that classification. Original Zeuthen text has not been directly checked here.

Related literature. Sur les différentes formes des courbes planes du quatrième ordre (H. G. Zeuthen, 1874). Historical attribution is retained here. The result’s sole article reference identifies the inspected statement or calculation at the recorded locator.

Source discussion. Theorem 1.7 and Table 1 give the six real quartic topological types and real bitangent counts 28,16,8,4,4,4. Thus every smooth real plane quartic has at least four real bitangent lines, and the minimum four is attained.
